trigger: a second replica's own migrate_from_sqlite backfill hits a legacy row whose id was already backfilled/seeded on Postgres by another replica, for any of the ~232 bundled definitions / 10 bundled sets every replica independently seeds during normal boot
summary: migrate_from_sqlite's backfill conflict check compared created_at (definitions) / the full row (sets) as write-once IDENTITY; a bundled row's created_at is stamped at replica-local first-seed time, not authored content, so it legitimately diverges across independently-provisioned replicas' legacy files for the exact same id — bricking the boot of every replica after the first to backfill any given bundled id

trigger: schedule_runner.cpp's fire() hits an InstructionStore DB-error/lease-timeout while resolving the definition to dispatch
summary: fire() called advance_schedule(s.id) on a genuine DB-error branch, permanently losing the scheduled occurrence instead of retrying it next tick; independently found by security-guardian and sre

trigger: two legacy replica files agree on a definition/set id AND created_by (e.g. a shared login used across pre-Postgres replicas, or hand-synced YAML that drifted) but disagree on content (yaml_source / name+description)
summary: 545936eb1's fix for gov1-backfill-identity narrowed IDENTITY to id/created_by-only, which itself over-corrected: it removed protection against two genuinely-different operator-authored rows sharing an id and created_by, silently discarding one side's real content with no log line naming the discard

trigger: insert_set_row's seed-path with_txn_for failure, and delete_set's post-txn failure
summary: 2 write-path DB-error branches (insert_set_row seed path, delete_set post-txn) did not call note_write_degrade, undercounting yuzu_server_instruction_write_degrade_total for those failure modes; independently found by cpp-safety and unhappy-path (UP-3)

trigger: PUT /api/instructions/{id} for an id that does not exist
summary: update_definition's not_found-prefixed error fell through to the route's bare 400 branch (indistinguishable from a validation failure) instead of the 404 every sibling route (DELETE, POST /import) in this migration uses; docs/user-manual/rest-api.md's PUT section also omitted the 404 case entirely

trigger: instruction.create/update/delete denial branches added in afb2b3824
summary: the 4 new create/update/delete denial audit_log calls discarded the [[nodiscard]] bool return via (void) instead of checking it and setting Sec-Audit-Failed on failure, per audit_log's own R2/#1073/PR#883 contract for security-relevant paths — the sibling POST /import route already followed the checked pattern

trigger: dispatch_due and evaluate_now claim the same policy id within the same wall-clock second (concurrent background tick + manual Evaluate Now, or two rapid manual triggers)
summary: the throttle-restore-on-store-unavailable CAS used the claim timestamp itself as the compare token; two claims on the same policy within the same second are indistinguishable, so a concurrent claim's restore could in theory clobber a different claim's throttle state — independently found by security-guardian, cpp-safety and unhappy-path (UP-2)

trigger: audit result/detail strings across instruction_store-adjacent routes (create_set/delete_set have no audit coverage at all; other routes use differing detail vocabularies)
summary: audit coverage and detail-string vocabulary for InstructionStore's REST routes is inconsistent (create_set/delete_set have zero audit logging, pre-existing and unrelated to this migration); a repo-wide convention question, not scoped to fix here

ADR-0058's Consequences section did not document afb2b3824's behaviour changes (schedule_runner retry-not-advance, policy_evaluator CAS/verdict_for changes, 7 new audit rows, persist_templates/uninstall_fn reclassification)

trigger: the 2 backfill regression tests' Catch2 tags
summary: tags were ordered [instruction_store][pg][backfill], inconsistent with the file's convention of putting [pg] last (e.g. [sets][pg])

trigger: any bundled definition's yaml_source legitimately drifts across release vintages and a second replica backfills it (the ordinary multi-replica upgrade case)
summary: c2c1018ca's kBundledDefinitionCreator was set to "" on the mistaken assumption that embed_content.py omits created_by for bundled definitions; def_envelope() actually sets created_by="system" unconditionally on every generated envelope (verified against embed_content.py source and every entry in the built bundled_content.cpp), so the sentinel-match/WARN branch was dead code for definitions and any ordinary yaml_source drift on a bundled definition took the fail-closed path, bricking the boot exactly like the original gov1-backfill-identity bug the fix commit's own title claimed to prevent. The existing regression test did not catch it because it only diverged on created_at (LIFECYCLE, ignored regardless of the sentinel value).

trigger: docs/adr/0058-instruction-store-postgres-migration.md's "Known residual" paragraph as written in c2c1018ca
summary: the documented residual named create_definition's REST route under RBAC-off/unauthenticated create as the trigger for an operator row colliding with the bundled sentinel; traced and found not reachable (require_permission/resolve_session's RBAC-off fallback still requires a valid session, every session-synthesis path sets a non-empty username). The actually-reachable trigger is POST /api/instructions/import, which sets created_by straight from the request body with no session override, under ordinary RBAC-enabled operation.

trigger: a backfill conflict check compares the existing Postgres yaml_source (read raw, since insert_definition_row/update_definition store it unsanitized to preserve exact Ed25519-signed bytes) against a freshly sanitize_pg_text'd legacy value
summary: raw-vs-sanitized comparison asymmetry, the same class that caused a false content mismatch in ProductPackStore (test_product_pack_store.cpp:698); not currently exploitable (sanitize_pg_text is idempotent and every persisted value already passed Postgres's own UTF8 validation at insert time, per E6) but fragile against a future relaxed validation path — made symmetric

the 404 body echoes update_definition's raw "not_found: " prefix operator-facing, unlike the #402 conflict-prefix-stripping precedent elsewhere in the file; take-or-leave per reviewer, docs/user-manual/rest-api.md already documents the shape deliberately

independently confirmed correct, no defect: note_write_degrade bracing at both new sites, PUT 404 db_error/not_found/validation classification, all 5 audit_log Sec-Audit-Failed checks, and the policy_evaluator generation-counter CAS (locking, TOCTOU, wraparound)

targeted re-verify of 99e3ab90f (the reverify1-bundled-def-sentinel-wrong fix) confirmed clean on all 4 points via independent empirical checks, not just reading: reverted the sentinel to '' and reran the new yaml_source-divergence test live against Postgres, confirming it fails exactly as claimed (red), then restored and reran the full [instruction_store][backfill][pg] suite green (96 assertions); fuzzed sanitize_pg_text idempotency over 200k random byte strings (0 mismatches) to validate the raw-vs-sanitized symmetry fix introduces no new false-mismatch; independently traced require_auth/resolve_session to confirm the ADR's corrected residual claim (RBAC-off unauthenticated create is unreachable, POST /api/instructions/import is the real reachable trigger). One NICE-only informational note, not gating: a human account literally named 'system' could also reach the sentinel via the ordinary create_definition route — same caller-influenced-created_by class the ADR already discloses, pre-existing, untouched by this commit.
